correctness.rationale: The equality configurations are precisely 105 disjoint free O(4) orbits by the cited published-preprint extremizer theorem. In each local face chamber, signed pyramids give an exact determinant for the eight-point hull; its intrinsic second variation is positive on 18 normal directions with quadratic coefficients 1/6 (12 modes) and 1/3 (6 modes). The O(4) orbit metric volume 2048 pi^4 and ellipsoid integral pi^9 6^6 3^3/9! divided by ambient (2 pi^2)^8 evaluate to 2916/pi^3. Compactness eliminates all other sublevel sources; dominated convergence justifies asymptotics. Local determinant identity independently numerically checked on 270 perturbations. Global theorem certificates are not independently checked; no false universal finite-scale claim is made.

originality.rationale: The exact ninth-power probability tail and coefficient are neither statements nor mathematical consequences of the inspected extremizer theorem, which supplies only the endpoint and equality locus, nor of the random S^2 expectation/deficiency formulas. The local 18-dimensional Hessian, metric orbit volume, and 105 matchings are explicitly calculated and compared against indexed findings by implication. Classical tube calculus is acknowledged as common method, so the claim is a specialized constant rather than invention of that method. Residual priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: Older or unindexed fixed-vertex random-polytope endpoint asymptotic literature could contain the same specialized coefficient.

value.rationale: A newly resolved global eight-vertex maximum naturally raises the tail-frequency question for fixed-sample sphere-generated polytopes. The exact ninth power and 2916/pi^3 constant constitute a geometric probability endpoint invariant, not an expected-value restatement. Evaluation requires precise normal curvature, continuous symmetry-orbit volume, and discrete matching multiplicity. The formula gives a nontrivial benchmark for extreme random inscribed polytopes with eight sample points.
